fixed_global_transition_model.name: ORIGINAL_FIXED_POINT_LOGIC_WITH_RANK
fixed_global_transition_model.semantics: Fixed-point logic extended by distinct rank operators rk_p for each prime field F_p, as in the original rank-logic proposal. Every finite formula/program can mention only finitely many such fixed-prime rank operators; no uniform prime-as-input rank operator is available.
fixed_global_transition_model.relation_to_R44AG: FPR strictly strengthens FPC and can express solvability of linear systems over fixed finite fields, so it repairs the specific affine/GF(2) expressiveness gap used in R44AG.

published_theorem.title: Rank Logic is Dead, Long Live Rank Logic!
published_theorem.statement_used: Extensions of FPC by rank operators over different prime fields are incomparable. Consequently original FPR, with a separate fixed rank operator for every prime field, fails to capture PTIME. In particular, the uniform rank problem—computing/deciding matrix rank when the finite-field prime is part of the input—is not expressible in original FPR, while it is polynomial-time computable.
published_theorem.successor_language: FPR* adds a uniform rank operator taking the prime/field information uniformly and is strictly more expressive than original FPR.

derived_TRUMP_barrier.claim: A universal TRUMP implicit decision/progress semantics exhausted by original FPR cannot discharge L1/L2, even though it restores fixed-field affine solvability absent from FPC.
reason: Original FPR can use rank over any prime field named in the finite formula, so it is genuinely stronger than R44AG's FPC model.
The cited theorem nevertheless separates original FPR from PTIME by the uniform rank problem.
Therefore fixed-prime rank access is not a universal global invariant language: field-uniform algebraic information remains outside the model.
A purported universal TRUMP language cannot discard a polynomial-time algebraic operation merely because its field parameter varies with the input.

dead_zone_mapping.meaning: Having arbitrarily many operators available in the language schema does not mean one finite program can uniformly select unbounded input-dependent field characteristics.

open_successor_boundary.rule: Do not inherit the original-FPR barrier. FPR* must be evaluated by its own current theorems. Absence of a known barrier in this artifact is not evidence that FPR* captures PTIME or solves 3SAT.

what_is_not_proved: No inexpressibility result for FPR* is claimed here.
No lower bound is claimed for algorithms with ordinary uniform finite-field linear algebra.
No claim is made that rank operators are insufficient ingredients for a future stronger language.

next_admissible_math.question: What is the strongest currently proved boundary for FPR* or another precisely fixed uniform-rank global model, and does that boundary yield a theorem-level obstacle to L1/L2/L3? If no such theorem is known, record OPEN rather than inventing a barrier.
forbidden: transferring FPR lower bounds to FPR* without proof
